subject: platform/daily
professional: a release/engineering-operations analyst who writes a daily status brief for an engineering manager; first questions: do the merge counts, line counts and run/cost figures match the system of record, is missing data said to be missing rather than zero, and does the same input always give the same text?

evidence.correctness: Ran collect.mjs readMerges/summariseRuns/parseMessage/areaOf/editionDays and progress.mjs against this checkout and recomputed with other tools. (1) Merges per day: readMerges gave 50 merges (6 on 11-07, 44 on 11-08 on HEAD); `git log --first-parent --format=%ct | date -u -d @t | uniq -c` gave the same 6/44; on origin/main, progress.mjs --cadence=daily --end=2026-11-07 reported 24 and the same git/date pipeline gave 24. (2) Lines: tool total +131281/-114 over the 50 merges; an awk sum over `git log --numstat` restricted to the 49 non-boundary commits gave 131281/114 exactly; including the shallow boundary commit awk gives 7671323 added, i.e. the tool correctly refuses to count the boundary commit (stats_unknown) rather than report 7.5M lines. (3) Run records for 2026-11-07: node summariseRuns gave 200 runs, success 176 / partial 24, 24 measured, $27.94; an independent Python json script gave 200, same outcomes, $27.94. (4) build.mjs facts.json for 11-07 (200 runs, $27.94) agreed. (5) parseMessage on a hand-made squash message gave the right title/PR/model/track/first sentence; firstSentence('Version 1.2 is out. Next.') returns 'Version 1.2 is out.' (decimal handled); editionDays for 11-08 gives 11-07, 11-06, 11-05. Not checked: Listen (browser speech), live site (proxy), the word-of-the-day / leaderboard prose beyond tests.
evidence.completeness: README claims checked: two daily write-ups (brief and Merge Report) built by build.mjs - works, 7 editions, index, show/, facts.json and feed.xml per day written; sources git/runs/decision queue/stats.json - git and runs work, asks and stats are optional and show as missing when absent (snapshot: no); progress.mjs daily/3day/weekly fact sheet - daily run end to end; usage-report.mjs covered by its own tests (3 pass) and USAGE_REPORT.md; ~2,400-word trim covered by a test. Listen player is in render output and tested for presence only (not run in a browser). No TODO/stub found in 1,756 lines. Build selects git ref HEAD while progress.mjs defaults to origin/main, so the two disagree on a local checkout (6 vs 24 merges for 11-07); undocumented but both are right for their ref.
evidence.verification: `node --test platform/daily/*.test.mjs`: 23 pass, 0 fail, ~0.9 s. Five hand-seeded mutations in core logic of collect.mjs, each reverted by copying a backup (git status of platform/ clean afterwards): (a) catalogue-wide sweep threshold `products.size >= 4` -> `>= 5`: caught (1 fail); (b) baseline rounding `Math.round(prior*10)/10` -> `Math.round(prior)`: caught (1 fail); (c) editionDays `(i+1)*DAY` -> `i*DAY` (includes the incomplete current day): caught (7 fail); (d) areaOf research-directory filter `!/^[_.]/.test(parts[1])` -> true: caught (1 fail); (e) shallow-boundary guard `shallow.has(sha) ? [] : stat` -> always parse stat: NOT caught, 23 pass, so a shallow clone would silently report millions of lines added and every file as newly added. Tests use hand-built merges for most facts, with few that exercise git against a shallow checkout.
evidence.craft: Read collect.mjs (316 lines), progress.mjs (211), build.mjs (65), and skimmed compose.mjs/render.mjs and tests. Strengths: pure functions with injected clock and ref, git invoked with execFileSync (no shell), deterministic templates, sorted tie-breaks, a deliberate shallow-clone guard, escaping in render. Defects: revert regex `/^Revert\b/i` is anchored but fix_forward regex `\b(fix(es)?|repair|unbreak)\b.*\bmain\b` matches any subject containing fix ... main (e.g. 'fix the main page layout' counts as main being red) and is presented in the Merge Report as 'the plot twist'; rename handling `p.replace(/\{[^}]*=> ([^}]*)\}/, '$1')` for `dir/{a => b}/f` yields `dir/b/f` only when no empty side, but `{ => sub}` leaves a double slash (not tested); silent catch blocks in readRuns and the shallow-file read; the base URL default in build.mjs is the retired github.io address; readMerges reads everything with a 512 MB buffer, fine here but unbounded.
evidence.claims: Checked: 'words come from templates, not a model, same facts same script' - test 'show is stable for a day', true; 'a source missing from a build is said to be missing, never shown as zero' - snapshot null when no stats, asks null, runs api_usd null when none measured, true; 'trims detail until it fits ~2,400 words' - test 'a huge day is trimmed', true; 'each has a facts.json and both kinds are in feed.xml' - build output contains both, true; 'rebuilt from git each time, no stored state' - true; Listen uses Web Speech with nothing uploaded - render has no network calls in test, but playback not run. Weaker: README links to duncan-haywood.github.io, which owner notes now redirects to marisstella.app (CLAUDE.md, Hosting); README does not say that build.mjs uses HEAD while progress.mjs uses origin/main, nor that fix-forward/revert flags are keyword heuristics. Disclaimer text present in rendered pages (2 matches).
evidence.fitness: Job: an engineering manager wants to know what merged yesterday, what is stuck and what the agent fleet spent. Walked through build.mjs for 7 days: briefs and show generated in seconds, 4-minute brief on 6 merges and 200 runs, numbers matched recomputation, missing CI snapshot stated. progress.mjs gives a fact sheet a post-writing session can use directly. Limits: facts are counts and titles, so 'most interesting' needs the human/agent judgment layer, which the README says; in a shallow clone the oldest day can silently lose stats (flagged by stats_unknown only in data).
evidence.domain: Compared with practice for engineering status reporting (DORA-style throughput reporting, release notes by area). Merges per day and lines per merge are volume measures, and the brief labels them as such; area attribution by touched-file majority with a noise filter is sensible, and the reverts/fix-forwards 'plot twist' is a rough stability proxy built on keyword matching rather than linking a fix to the commit it fixes. A release manager would use it as a changelog digest but would not read the fix-forward count as a change-failure rate, and lines added is a weak proxy for work (7.5M-line import commits dominate if not excluded). Stated limits are thin.

defects.what: The shallow-clone boundary guard (stats_unknown, files/lines treated as unknown) has no test: removing it leaves all 23 tests green, and the result would report the whole repository as added in one merge.
fix_forward is a keyword regex over subject and first body paragraph; any subject like 'fix the main page' counts as main being red, and the Merge Report presents it as the day's plot twist.
build.mjs reads git ref HEAD while progress.mjs defaults to origin/main; on a local checkout the same day gave 6 vs 24 merges. Not documented.
README and build.mjs default base URL point at the retired duncan-haywood.github.io address (CI overrides via PAGES_BASE_URL).
Rename path rewrite handles only some numstat brace forms (`{ => sub}` leaves a double slash); untested. Silent catch blocks in readRuns and shallow-file read.

verdict: A small, deterministic, honestly-labelled digest generator whose arithmetic I could reproduce: merges per day (6/44 on HEAD, 24 on origin/main), line totals (+131281/-114, with the shallow boundary commit correctly excluded) and run counts and cost (200 runs, $27.94) all matched independent git/awk/Python recomputation. 23 tests pass and four of five seeded mutations were caught, but removing the shallow-boundary guard went unnoticed. Weaknesses are keyword-based fix-forward flags shown as facts, a HEAD versus origin/main difference between its two entry points, and a stale hosting URL in the README. It meets the bar (correctness, claims, verification all 3; median 3) without room to spare. Listen playback and the live site were not exercised.
